### OpenCode TUI: Use `linefeed` Instead of `ctrl+j` for `input_submit`

In my tests with Windows Terminal and XShell 8 using `showkey -a`:

| Key | Raw input | OpenTUI event |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter | `\r` (`0x0d`) | `return` |
| Shift+Enter | `\r` (`0x0d`) | `return` |
| Ctrl+M | `\r` (`0x0d`) | `return` |
| Ctrl+Enter | `\n` (`0x0a`) | `linefeed` |
| Ctrl+J | `\n` (`0x0a`) | `linefeed` |

OpenTUI parses raw `\n` as `linefeed`, which Textarea maps to a newline.

To make Enter insert a newline and Ctrl+Enter submit, use:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "keybinds": {
    "input_newline": "return",
    "input_submit": "linefeed"
  }
}
```

Result:

- Enter, Shift+Enter, and Ctrl+M insert a newline.
- Ctrl+Enter and Ctrl+J submit the prompt.

No terminal remapping is needed for this raw CR/LF setup. Distinguishing Ctrl+Enter from Ctrl+J requires the terminal to send a distinct sequence, such as CSI-u.

Version note: this was tested with OpenCode `v1.18.25`, which uses OpenTUI `v0.4.5`. The same behavior remains in OpenTUI `v0.5.9`.

Relevant OpenTUI v0.5.9 source:

- [`\r` / `\n` parsing](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.5.9/packages/core/src/lib/parse.keypress.ts#L360-L367)
- [`linefeed -> newline` default binding](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.5.9/packages/core/src/renderables/Textarea.ts#L94-L98)
- [Custom bindings take precedence over textarea defaults](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/v0.5.9/packages/keymap/src/addons/opentui/edit-buffer-bindings.ts#L350-L357)

Clarifying how this differs from the linked duplicates, plus fresh log evidence from the local setup (wanted to add data before checking the bot's dedup suggestions).

## How this is distinct

- **#42956** (big-pickle stuck in autoregressive loop during *brainstorming*): same model, but the stuck phase there is generation during an open-ended creative task. This report is the **closing/persistence phase** — the model has *already decided* on concrete actionable steps (write backup, edit, then a tool call) and still cannot emit the tool.
- **#45442** (infinite loop of *identical tool calls*): here the model emits **no tool calls at all** — it loops on *text generation / re-requesting the LLM* instead of calling tools. The opposite failure of the tool-call-repetition loop.
- **#26220** (infinite loop *after tool calls complete*): that is post-tool stagnation. This report is **pre-tool** — narration without ever issuing the call.

So the distinguishing signature: **repeated LLM `stream` calls with zero tool emissions**, and it does **not self-recover** (needs a manual abort).

## Log evidence (2026-08-28, opencode 1.18.22, Ubuntu 24.04/WSL2)

From `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`, all in a single run `a9c7879c`, model `opencode/big-pickle`, agent `plan`:

**1. Narration loop without tool calls (00:58–01:01):**
- 8 consecutive `message=stream` events for `big-pickle` within ~3 minutes.
- Between those streams: **0 real tool calls** (only the initial `shell tool using shell` before the window).
- The first stream (00:58:08) was cut and needed a **manual abort** (`level=ERROR ... error=Aborted` at 00:58:11) — it did not exit the loop on its own.

**2. Recurring burst (16:05–16:09):**
- ~28 consecutive `big-pickle` streams in 4 minutes with **only 1 `permission=bash` event** and **0 errors** → chained text generation without acting.

**3. Global frequency (that day):**
- **523 `stream` LLM calls for `big-pickle` in this single run** (all other runs that day total 13). Peak of 10 streams/minute at 16:06.
- Streams are 3–15 s apart, i.e. short generation turns with no tool side effects — matching the "narration/no-op" signature.

Volunteer data for whoever triages: happy to share the session/snapshot or a larger log excerpt. This is the same *platform* as #42950 (which just got a Windows confirmation), so it may be worth correlating the two — both involve `opencode/big-pickle` (and adjacent free models) stalling or degrading on the built-in provider.

Adding the **root cause hypothesis** and a **minimal reproduction** — this is what I believe the runtime/loop actually does, so it can be fixed faster. Based on the same log data.

## Observed mechanism (what the logs show)

Following one `stream` in the burst, the loop advances one integer per iteration:

```
loop step=47   →  stream (big-pickle)  →  no tool-call part  →  loop step=48  →  stream …
loop step=48   →  stream (big-pickle)  →  no tool-call part  →  loop step=49  →  stream …
… (repeats)
```

- Each agent-loop iteration issues **exactly one LLM `stream` call** for `big-pickle`.
- The response contains **no `tool` part** (no `tool-call`), only text; so the runtime has nothing to execute and just **iterates the loop again**.
- Timing: `loop step=N → stream` is 3–15 s apart; a truly-working step would show a tool execution/permission event between iterations. In the bursts there is **none**.
- Global proof: the whole closing run did **556 loop steps** (max `step=69` per-part counter; 100s of `stream` calls). A closing task of this size (backup + edit + write + mine) should be well under ~40 steps. The rest was consumed by narration with no-op turns.

## Root cause hypothesis

The model enters a **degenerate text-generation attractor**: with the decision already made and the correct next tool known, it keeps producing prose that *describes* the tool call instead of the tool call itself. Because the assistant turn ends with a text part and no `tool` part, the runtime correctly has nothing to run and re-enters the loop — so **the harness is obeying the agent-loop contract, but the model never completes a turn with a tool call**. Two contributing factors to check:

1. **Context pressure at end-of-session**: this appeared at the closing/persistence phase of a long session (many prior steps, big accumulated context). Compare with the mimicry in #42950 (free-model degradation) — likely correlated.
2. **No loop protection for "text-only turns"**: there is protection for repeated *tool calls* (#45442) but I don't see one for repeated **tool-less** turns. A guard that detects N consecutive assistant turns with no tool call (e.g. "no-progress" / "narration-only") and stops/retries would bound the blast radius regardless of model.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Any session where the agent has a **decided, single next tool call** (e.g. closing a session: `write file X`, then a tool call), ideally late in a long session.
2. Let `big-pickle` drive the last steps.
3. Observe: assistant emits text narrating the action; no `tool` part; `loop step` monotonically increments; repeats until manually aborted.

## Suggested fix / ask

1. **Loop guard**: detect N consecutive assistant turns that return **text-only with no tool call and no final answer**, then surface a warning / stop (mirroring the existing tool-call loop protection).
2. **Log the no-op**: log a `no-tool-part` signal so it's countable in a dashboard (like the stream-error buckets).
3. Verify whether end-of-session context length triggers it (compare a long vs short session).

Happy to share the full session snapshot or a redacted log excerpt on request.

### Additional reproduction from Kali Linux — `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`

Confirming this on `opencode-go/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`. Same signature as the
original report: `GET /zen/go/v1/models` returns 200, but every `POST` to
`/chat/completions` returns 500 at the Cloudflare edge.

**Environment**
- OS: Kali Linux
- opencode: v1.18.25
- Provider/model: `opencode-go` / `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` (free)
- Region: Iraq

**Direct curl reproduction**

Valid API key, explicit `reasoning.effort: "medium"` — instant HTTP 500:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"muse-spark-1.2-contributor","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"reasoning":{"effort":"medium"}}'
```

Response:

```http
HTTP/2 500
date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:09:03 GMT
content-type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8
server: cloudflare
cf-ray: a33cf442afea7a8c-CLT

{"type":"error","error":{"type":"error","message":"Internal server error"}}
```

Note the `content-type: text/plain` on a JSON body — consistent with the edge
generating this response rather than the upstream model service.

**Ruled out locally**
- Auth token valid; network path healthy.
- Disabled local MCP servers (`kali`, `kali-tools`) — no change.

**Client-side symptom**

In the TUI the request hangs with the spinner running, then flips to
`interrupted` with no error surfaced, while local context is still consumed.
This matches the "sub-agent timeout, no error" behaviour described in the
original report, and is likely amplified by the unbounded 5xx retry policy
tracked in #25041.

**Separate finding (possibly unrelated to the 500)**

From `~/.local/share/opencode/log/`, the background title generator sends
`reasoning.effort: "none"`, which this model rejects with a 400:

```
[invalid_request_error] "reasoning.effort" does not support "none" with this model.
```

Filing here for visibility since it also affects `muse-*`, but it is a distinct
failure class from the gateway 500 above. Happy to open it separately if
preferred.

**Question**

Is the 500 region-gated? `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` is documented as
"available in select regions", and #43692 shows a `RegionError` for
unsupported countries. If the gateway is collapsing that check into a generic
500, a clearer error would save a lot of debugging time.

There is something weird happening, while i was sleeping and no api keys were being used, there were made some petitions with kimi and other models that i don´t use, maxing out my account.

+1 on Linux (x86-64, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS), opencode v1.18.25. Reproduced the same idle high-CPU pattern.

Symptom while the session is fully idle (no active request, no streaming, no file activity):

- Main thread sits at ~50% of one core, `STAT=Rl+` (running, not sleeping), WCHAN cycling through `ep_poll`.
- The Bun `HeapHelper` thread sits at ~20-25% on `futex` — appears to be GC pressure driven by the main-loop churn.
- No active network connections and no inotify event traffic at the time, so the spin is internal, not I/O-driven.

This matches the `epoll_pwait(..., timeout=0)` busy-loop signature already reported in #24719 and #15600 — the `runEventSubscription()` reconnect loop in `packages/opencode/src/acp/agent.ts` with no backoff, and the broken-socket handling in `http-server.ts` / `instance-events.ts`. The main loop appears to poll with a zero timeout and immediately re-enters instead of blocking. The empty-string spin in `MultiOccurrenceReplacer` (`packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts`) is a related event-loop-blocking path.

Killing and restarting the affected session is the only reliable workaround (consistent with #21889's findings). A proper fix would have the event loop block with a non-zero timeout / sleep when no events are pending, and add backoff to the reconnect path.

Happy to provide more detail if useful. Would be great to know if a fix is planned for this, since it's been reported across several versions and platforms.

A per-model wire hint doesn't solve this for protocol-locked clients like Codex.

The gateway boundary should be:

`client protocol -> canonical semantics -> working backend protocol`

Here that means Codex keeps speaking Responses while mimo/glm/ox-alpha are lowered to Chat Completions. #44659 demonstrates the inverse case, so protocol clearly isn't a model property either.

This is exactly the class of problem we built [swobuforge/swobu](https://github.com/swobuforge/swobu) around: Responses and Chat are independent on each side of the gateway, with tools/reasoning translated between them.

Model availability really needs to be `(model, protocol, capabilities)`, not just `model`.

I traced the gap in the code. Title generation (`packages/core/src/session/title.ts`) does publish a `SessionEvent.UsageRecorded` with `source: "title"` on step finish, so the token/cost *are* recorded as events. The problem is on the aggregation side: `packages/core/src/session/stats.ts` only folds `UsageRecorded` events into session cost when `json_extract(data, '$.source') = 'compaction'` (line ~296). The `source: "title"` records are therefore excluded from the session/stats cost totals, which is exactly the understatement described here.

The fix is small and scoped to the stats aggregation: include the `title` source alongside `compaction` so these hidden title-generation calls show up in session cost/usage.

I'll implement this against `v2` with a regression test and open a PR linked to this issue.

+1 to this — I hit the exact case `steer` is meant for in the CLI (TUI) today:

The agent was working on a task, went off in the wrong direction, and I sent a corrective prompt. That prompt just sat in the queue while the agent kept going down the rabbit hole, because there's no way to say "deliver this **now**, as steering for the running turn". My only options were to wait it out or hit interrupt and resend — the queued message itself had no way to be promoted.

Concretely, what would fix this for me:

- A **steer action attached to the queued message itself** (e.g. a keybind/button like ctrl+s or a `Steer` control on the pending prompt in the TUI) that interrupts the current turn at a safe boundary and injects that queued message as steering input for the next turn — instead of waiting for the current (wrong) work to finish.
- This is subtly different from a global `steer` default mode: I want `queue` to remain the default behavior, but with an explicit escape hatch per queued prompt when I can see the agent is going the wrong way.

Happy to help prototype a patch for the TUI side of this (queued-prompt → steer promotion) if that's useful.

Status update: #45994 addressed the primary resource-amplification scenario demonstrated here.

Session-family hydration of pending forms and permissions now uses atomic optional acquisition for `session.form.list` and `session.permission.list`, returning an empty collection for an unloaded Location rather than constructing its runtime. The special global-form list path received the same treatment. This prevents polling historical sessions from creating the runtime graphs, watchers, plugins, MCP processes, and child-process growth described in the reproduction.

The broader passive-read invariant and endpoint audit in this issue remain incomplete. In particular, the listed metadata reads, location-wide pending-request reads, individual form and permission reads, PTY reads, and shell reads have not all been converted to lightweight or existing-runtime-only acquisition.

Accordingly, #45994 resolves the primary observed failure mode but only partially resolves this issue's expanded scope.

Also hitting this on opencode web (1.18.5, Docker). Images returned by MCP tools are converted to `data:` URIs in `session/tools.ts` and stored in `part.state.attachments`; they reach the model correctly, but the chat UI never renders them, so the only way to look at a screenshot a tool just produced is to open the file outside opencode.

This PR was closed by the automated cleanup rather than on review, and it already carries an independent verification against a Desktop build in the thread above. Could a maintainer either reopen it, or point at #39817 as the preferred direction so the effort isn't split across two patches?

Another concrete case for this: I drive a fairly large MCP stack from opencode web (1.18.5 in Docker), and several of those tools return screenshots.

The pipeline works right up to the last step. `session/tools.ts` turns MCP `image` content into a `data:<mime>;base64,…` attachment, it lands in `part.state.attachments`, the SDK exposes it on `SessionMessageToolStateCompleted`, and the model receives it. Only the UI drops it, so the images are invisible to the person sitting in front of the session — which is exactly the case where you want to see them.

Worth noting the same data path also covers the built-in `read` tool, which builds identical data URIs in `tool/read.ts`. A UI-side fix would therefore cover both without touching the server.

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.
